quarterly_data.signal: CFO Wissam Jabre added detail to the raised FY2027 guide: alongside the top-line raise NetApp 'also increased the operating margin guidance at the midpoint by around 120 basis points', and the second half guide is also higher than it was 90 days ago. At the midpoint, revenue now splits roughly 50/50 between first half and second half (slightly less than 50% in the first half), in line with the split of multiple prior years, so the implied back-half deceleration is the extra week in Q1 plus normal seasonality rather than a demand or supply signal.
quarterly_data.figure: increased the operating margin guidance at the midpoint by around 120 basis points

quarterly_data.signal: Component supply behind the doubled growth outlook: Jabre said NetApp has 'different types of arrangements with different types of suppliers. In some cases, we have LTAs. In others, we basically have agreed upon commitments' and that NetApp feels comfortable it has the supply to deliver the guided outlook. He added that for most of the commodities NetApp purchases it has more than one supplier, which helps secure supply and in some cases helps on cost. He also noted NetApp sells direct to end-customer demand, so there is no channel stocking inflating the order book.

Component cost inflation: 'we are operating in a tight supply chain environment, so it’s too early to make a call on the component pricing.' NetApp has been passing through component cost inflation 'for now a couple of quarters' and has built agility (e.g. shortening the duration of its quotes) to re-price faster when component costs rise. Product gross margin guided for Q2 through Q4 is slightly better than expected 90 days ago; the full-year gross margin guide is slightly lower only because of the richer product revenue mix.

Public cloud economics and durability: 'Public cloud margins, to be precise, in Q1 were at 86%+' against a long-term range of 80%-85% that NetApp has exceeded for three quarters and is choosing not to reset yet. Jabre called high-teens growth sustainable for the segment and disclosed that the first-party and marketplace portion of public cloud 'last year grew at around 31%', well above the segment. The three hyperscaler first-party customers - Microsoft, Google and AWS - are all growing at a nice pace though not all of equal size.
quarterly_data.figure: first-party and marketplace portion of the public cloud business last year grew at around 31%

quarterly_data.signal: Media mix nuance in the current component-inflation environment: hybrid flash (hard-disk based) revenue rose slightly year-on-year in Q1, the second quarter in a row after many quarters of decline, and NetApp called out strength in that business going forward. Management explicitly broke the old margin assumption: 'from a hybrid flash versus all-flash, we do not have much of a differential on the margin side', and IR added investors should not assume the historical relative margin performance of different product classes holds in this environment.
